sources.title: A Comprehensive Formal Security Analysis of OAuth 2.0
sources.finding: OAuth flow analysis separates authorization, authentication and session integrity; fixes depend on the modeled flow and attacker.
sources.decision: Keep the gateway a resource server; do not turn arbitrary OAuth tokens into login evidence or implement an embedded identity provider.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: The Web SSO Standard OpenID Connect
sources.finding: OIDC adds identity semantics and discovery/registration attack surfaces beyond OAuth. Its proof does not certify every implementation.
sources.decision: Pin issuer/JWKS and use local subject bindings; require access-token type when the issuer supports that profile.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: An Extensive Formal Security Analysis of the OpenID Financial-grade API
sources.finding: FAPI strengthens high-risk flows with token binding and explicit attacker assumptions. Its configurations are not interchangeable.
sources.decision: Reject cnf-bound tokens on the bearer path until the corresponding proof verifier exists.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: On the security of modern Single Sign-On Protocols: Second-Order Vulnerabilities in OpenID Connect
sources.finding: Malicious discovery endpoints can expose credentials in later protocol steps. The original-version title differs from later metadata.
sources.decision: Validate deployment-owned security URLs and disallow redirects; do not discover endpoints from unverified token fields.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: SPRESSO: A Secure, Privacy-Respecting Single Sign-On System for the Web
sources.finding: SPRESSO addresses identity-provider privacy through a separate SSO protocol and formal model. It is not a drop-in MCP verifier.
sources.decision: Avoid unnecessary token/payload retention; defer new SSO protocols to identity providers.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Cerberus: Query-driven Scalable Vulnerability Detection in OAuth Service Provider Implementations
sources.finding: The fetched original version is titled OAuthShield. Its static analyzer checks OAuth server implementation logic; later metadata calls it Cerberus.
sources.decision: Use adversarial verification tests; do not claim that using a library proves correct integration or that we ran this analyzer.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: A Gateway Architecture for Enterprise MCP Authentication
sources.finding: The experience paper separates user/non-user personas and execution credentials, with explicit service-account authorization. It also describes older password-grant patterns.
sources.decision: Add optional verified client_id binding; retain separate upstream credentials. Reject copying password grants merely because a paper deploys them.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Zero-Trust Authorization and Discovery for Enterprise MCP
sources.finding: The enterprise MCP paper proposes heterogeneous credential adapters and pre-auth discovery; its SDK comparisons are version specific.
sources.decision: Implement bounded RFC 7662 introspection, but retain authenticated catalog discovery rather than expose private schemas publicly.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Formal Security Analysis of the OpenID FAPI 2.0
sources.finding: FAPI 2.0 analysis finds interactions among PAR, DPoP, mTLS and issuer binding; security follows revised specifications and the model.
sources.decision: Treat proof-of-possession as a separate complete contract, not a certificate/proxy-header checkbox.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: O Single Sign-Off, Where Art Thou?
sources.finding: The empirical SSO study finds account/session access can outlive user remediation; observations cover its tested services and era.
sources.decision: No positive introspection cache in this release; require fresh checks and document JWT revocation limits.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Zanzibar
sources.finding: Zanzibar combines relation tuples, namespace policies and causal consistency; its production results depend on Google infrastructure.
sources.decision: Retain OpenFGA composition and HIGHER_CONSISTENCY; do not describe it as Zanzibar zookie or external-consistency equivalence.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Macaroons
sources.finding: Macaroons attenuate authority through contextual caveats, all of which must hold. Cryptographic delegation adds issuance/discharge/replay responsibilities.
sources.decision: Keep policies and inspectors narrowing-only; defer a new credential format.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Cedar
sources.finding: Cedar provides default denial, forbids overriding permits, deterministic evaluation and formal analysis. Its performance claims concern its compared implementations.
sources.decision: Add explicit argument deny rules that override allows; do not claim a Cedar engine or formal proof.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Efficient and Extensible Policy Mining for Relationship-Based Access Control
sources.finding: Feature selection focuses evolutionary ReBAC policy mining on promising attributes. Mining depends on supplied entitlement/object data.
sources.decision: Do not infer production permission grants from observed traffic or model suggestions.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: A Decision Tree Learning Approach for Mining Relationship-Based Access Control Policies
sources.finding: Decision-tree ReBAC mining balances consistency with source ACLs and structural complexity. Compact policies are not proof that source entitlements are correct.
sources.decision: Keep migration/review explicit and test denied cases, not only equivalent allowed cases.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Greedy and Evolutionary Algorithms for Mining Relationship-Based Access Control Policies
sources.finding: The retrieved body is titled Mining Relationship-Based Access Control Policies; greedy/generalization algorithms use an explicit class/object model.
sources.decision: Keep relationship modeling outside routing and preserve the deployed OpenFGA model pin.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Learning Attribute-Based and Relationship-Based Access Control Policies with Unknown Values
sources.finding: Unknown-value mining uses three-valued logic and experiments over incomplete entity data. It is an offline policy-learning setting.
sources.decision: Missing tenant, subject or client binding must not be filled in from guesses at request time.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Authentication and authorization in Data Spaces
sources.finding: ODRL compilation plus OpenFGA demonstrates a data-space use case; usage control and metadata privacy remain future work.
sources.decision: Keep gateway tool access separate from downstream usage control or record ownership claims.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: AutoCedar
sources.finding: AutoCedar fixes a reviewed semantic target before verifier-guided policy synthesis. Evaluation corpora and formal encodings bound its claims.
sources.decision: Keep publication review/revision gates; defer autonomous production policy synthesis.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: RAISE
sources.finding: RAISE trains policy synthesis against symbolic checks; synthetic targets, backbone choices and experimental seeds affect transfer.
sources.decision: Use executable positive/negative boundaries; do not grant live authority based on generated prose.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Maglev
sources.finding: Maglev balances network flows with consistent hashing and connection tracking. Packet throughput is not MCP call performance.
sources.decision: Retain stable application routing and test eligibility before selection; no throughput parity claim.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Slicer
sources.finding: Slicer separates forwarding from a control plane that manages assignments and load. It relies on deployment signals and coordination.
sources.decision: Keep routing behind a narrow plugin interface; do not run a planner in request dispatch.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Beamer
sources.finding: Beamer moves connection-state responsibility to backends to tolerate churn. It assumes transport/backend cooperation.
sources.decision: Do not confuse stateless MCP selection with migration of arbitrary legacy backend sessions.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Consistent Hashing and Random Trees
sources.finding: Consistent hashing minimizes remapping under membership changes, under an explicit caching/network model.
sources.decision: Retain membership-stability tests and avoid attaching authorization authority to affinity choices.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: A Fast, Minimal Memory, Consistent Hash Algorithm
sources.finding: Jump hashing is compact but assumes sequential bucket numbers, limiting arbitrary removals.
sources.decision: Retain weighted rendezvous for named target membership; do not add another strategy solely to increase feature counts.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Dynamo
sources.finding: Dynamo combines availability-oriented storage techniques and eventual consistency. Some workload details are aggregated.
sources.decision: Do not apply eventual-consistency permission caching to revocation; use shared revisions and explicit failures.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Analyzing Distributed Join-Idle-Queue
sources.finding: JIQ fluid-limit analysis identifies high-load variance and assumptions missing from simpler treatments.
sources.decision: Defer queue-aware dispatch until trustworthy shared load signals and measurements exist.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Optimal Rate-Matrix Pruning For Large-Scale Heterogeneous Systems
sources.finding: Rate-matrix pruning accounts for task/server heterogeneity with asymptotic assumptions. Faster-server heuristics can reduce stability.
sources.decision: Add explicit priority configuration, but do not call it adaptive or delay-optimal routing.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Join-Idle-Queue with Service Elasticity
sources.finding: Elastic JIQ stability is a large-system result; subcritical load alone does not ensure every finite system is stable.
sources.decision: Keep bounded concurrency and avoid claiming scalability from an algorithm name.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Heavy-traffic Delay Optimality in Pull-based Load Balancing Systems
sources.finding: Pull-based routing balances communication overhead and delay guarantees; local idle-state information can become stale.
sources.decision: Use configured trusted tenant/role selectors; defer local least-load decisions presented as cluster-wide truth.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Raft
sources.finding: Raft separates election, replication and safety in a crash-fault model. A gateway replica count is not itself a consensus system.
sources.decision: Use PostgreSQL for shared configuration; do not implement another consensus layer inside the gateway.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Paxos Made Simple
sources.finding: Paxos requires intersecting quorums and persistent proposal state; safety and progress are distinct.
sources.decision: Keep transactional revisions and deployment-owned database availability; no distributed exactly-once claim.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: The Tail at Scale
sources.finding: Tail-at-scale techniques distinguish within-request mitigation and longer-term adaptation; hedging can add load.
sources.decision: Add independent connection limits and cumulative upstream deadlines; do not hedge effectful calls.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Viewstamped Replication Revisited
sources.finding: Viewstamped replication distinguishes stale reads from causally constrained reads and lease assumptions.
sources.decision: Retain fresh shared-revision checks and explicit outage denial rather than stale authorization fallback.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Spanner
sources.finding: Spanner combines replication, transactions and clock uncertainty. TrueTime results are not available merely by using SQL.
sources.decision: Keep storage adapters loosely coupled; do not claim global external consistency for the local PostgreSQL deployment.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: The Chubby lock service
sources.finding: Chubby uses coarse-grained locks and fencing to protect against delayed work. Distributed locks require more than familiar local-lock intuition.
sources.decision: Retain bounded leases and no automatic effect replay; defer resource fencing until backend adapters enforce it.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Dapper
sources.finding: Dapper prioritizes low overhead, transparency and privacy; it deliberately avoids RPC payload logging.
sources.decision: Keep metadata-only tracing/audit; do not copy payload-capturing vendor defaults.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Large-scale cluster management at Google with Borg
sources.finding: Borg handles routine failures through placement, rescheduling and resource policies. Application correctness still requires durable state and failure handling.
sources.decision: Keep Kubernetes lifecycle separate from tool routing; smoke tests are not multi-node disruption certification.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Deconstructing the Tail at Scale Effect Across Network Protocols
sources.finding: The network tail study compares TCP/UDP/RDMA under a controlled experimental setup. It does not establish a universal benefit from changing protocols.
sources.decision: Keep standards-compliant MCP transports; defer arbitrary RDMA/WebSocket additions without protocol contracts.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: KedgeFlow: A Programmable Control Plane for Enterprise AI Agents
sources.finding: KedgeFlow binds approved requests to single-use shared claims and retains uncertain outcomes; the reference scope is a single-resource path.
sources.decision: Keep retries disabled for tool effects; stage independent approval, idempotency and reconciliation as a separate durable contract.
sources.scope: Selected design/threat/model and evidence/scope sections, with targeted follow-up. No complete proof audit or benchmark reproduction.

sources.title: Critical vulnerabilities in JSON Web Token libraries
sources.finding: Historical JWT library exploits show algorithm confusion and unsigned-token acceptance.
sources.decision: Retain the RS256/ES256 allowlist; add none/HMAC/signature-negative regression cases. The article is historical, not evidence of a current jose vulnerability.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Signing Algorithms Overview
sources.finding: Signing authenticates content but does not encrypt it; shared-key and public-key verification have different trust requirements.
sources.decision: Keep public-key verification at ingress and secrets out of token claims and logs. Do not implement cryptography locally.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Brute Forcing HS256 is Possible: The Importance of Using Strong Keys in Signing JWTs
sources.finding: Weak HMAC secrets permit offline guessing; the demonstrated timing depends on hardware and secret strength.
sources.decision: Do not add arbitrary HS256 configuration to this resource server. The test checks algorithm rejection, not brute-force resistance.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: ID Token and Access Token: What Is the Difference? | Auth0
sources.finding: ID tokens and access tokens have different recipients and purposes.
sources.decision: Keep issuer/audience checks and optional access-token typ profile. Allow explicit OAuth subjects without unused API keys; never accept them as API-key credentials.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Protect Your Access Tokens with DPoP
sources.finding: DPoP binds tokens to client keys and adds per-request proof semantics.
sources.decision: Keep rejecting cnf-bearing tokens until method/URL binding, nonce and cross-replica replay protection are implemented. DPoP does not solve malicious action by an already-authorized agent.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: On-Behalf-Of Is a Pattern. Token Exchange Is the Standard.
sources.finding: On-behalf-of is a delegation pattern; vendor grant formats and RFC 8693 are not interchangeable.
sources.decision: Require the returned issued_token_type for RFC 8693 exchange; reject ID-token output. Token exchange alone is not proof of user consent to an agent action.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Refresh Token Security: Detecting Hijacking and Misuse with Auth0
sources.finding: Refresh reuse can signal theft or a legitimate race; network and user-agent heuristics need false-positive handling.
sources.decision: Fix concurrent expired-cache exchanges. Keep interactive refresh-token storage/rotation at the identity service; do not infer compromise solely from IP changes.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Demystifying OAuth Security: State vs. Nonce vs. PKCE
sources.finding: State, nonce and PKCE protect different steps in interactive OAuth/OIDC flows.
sources.decision: Defer a hosted login flow until redirect/session/PKCE lifecycle is designed. These parameters are not substitutes for resource-server token validation.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Common Risks of Giving Your API Keys to AI Agents
sources.finding: Shared broad API keys obscure attribution and enlarge the impact of disclosure.
sources.decision: Support keyless OAuth-only identities, retain per-agent grants and separate upstream credentials. A vault does not itself prevent prompt injection or unauthorized decisions.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens and The Principle of Least Privilege
sources.finding: Least privilege requires resource binding, appropriate scopes and limited token lifetime.
sources.decision: Reject an explicitly narrowed token response missing requested scopes. Omitted scope does not automatically mean unlimited access; local grants still constrain every call.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Understanding ReBAC and ABAC Through OpenFGA and Cedar
sources.finding: OpenFGA relationships and Cedar attributes organize authorization data differently; either requires trustworthy and fresh inputs.
sources.decision: Retain the replaceable Authorizer interface and OpenFGA adapter. Do not add Cedar merely to duplicate existing argument constraints.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: How To Evaluate Resource-Specific Permissions Efficiently with ReBAC instead of RBAC
sources.finding: Resource-specific rights can grow awkwardly when encoded as many global roles or token claims.
sources.decision: Keep group-to-tool relationships in OpenFGA and backend record ownership at the backend unless a trusted resource-binding design is introduced.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: What Is Relationship-based access control (ReBAC)
sources.finding: Relationships are facts; permissions derive from a model and may require multiple graph traversals.
sources.decision: Pin the model, use higher consistency and fail closed on dependency faults. Do not equate a relationship tuple with an unconditional permission.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Policy Testing With Oso Cloud - Part 1: Local Testing
sources.finding: Fast local policy checks complement service integration tests; syntax validation alone does not prove intended decisions.
sources.decision: Add a local permission-intersection matrix and retain real OpenFGA grant/inheritance/revocation tests. No dependency on a paid Oso service is introduced.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Building the GitHub Authorization Model Using oso - oso
sources.finding: Repository and organization roles differ, and permission inheritance can be expressed through recursive model rules.
sources.decision: Keep inheritance in the external relationship model rather than copying a fixed GitHub hierarchy into the gateway. Test local/role/relationship intersection.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Test driving “power of two random choices” load balancing
sources.finding: Power-of-two selection depends on a load signal; multiple independent balancers and slow-start complicate comparisons.
sources.decision: Defer least-load routing until reliable metrics and lifecycle hooks exist. Do not market a process-local counter as global capacity.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Client IP Persistence or Source IP Hash Load Balancing
sources.finding: Naive source hashing can remap broadly on membership changes; persistence tables and consistent hashing have different costs.
sources.decision: Retain principal-based rendezvous for stable assignment. Avoid IP-based identity, particularly behind NAT and proxies.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Two ways to enable sticky sessions in HAProxy (guide)
sources.finding: Cookies and source IP offer different session-affinity tradeoffs; NAT and changing addresses skew IP affinity.
sources.decision: Keep agent identity as the affinity key and document that affinity is not resumability or guaranteed session migration.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Load Balancing with Weighted Pools | Cloudflare Blog
sources.finding: Relative weights support canaries and capacity splits; removing a pool from selection is useful during maintenance.
sources.decision: Add explicit enabled:false per route target across all built-in strategies. It pauses alias selection; separately granted direct tools remain available.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Rich, complex rules for advanced load balancing | Cloudflare Blog
sources.finding: Rule-based steering supports business and location needs, but a broad expression language adds semantics and trust requirements.
sources.decision: Retain trusted tenant/role/client selectors and the Router plugin. Extend continuation eligibility to check those selectors and disabled targets; defer arbitrary caller-header trust.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: The complete guide to Go net/http timeouts | Cloudflare Blog
sources.finding: Different HTTP phases and streaming traffic need distinct budgets; fixed deadlines and idle timeouts are not interchangeable.
sources.decision: Retain total upstream budgets including credential acquisition and separate connection limits. Add bounded JWKS reads using the existing deadline. Go-specific APIs are not copied into Node.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Bringing insights into TCP resets and timeouts to Cloudflare Radar | Cloudflare Blog
sources.finding: Early TCP resets/timeouts can have multiple causes, including client behavior, middleboxes and attacks.
sources.decision: Do not infer that a tool action failed or retry it solely from a reset. Distinguish transport observations from execution outcomes.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.

sources.title: Google SRE - Cascading Failures: Reducing System Outage
sources.finding: Retry and failover feedback can turn partial overload into a cascading failure.
sources.decision: Keep effect retries disabled and preserve quotas, circuits, bounded fan-out and cancellation tests. Capacity/soak validation remains separate work.
sources.scope: Selected explanatory, design, limitation and operational paragraphs inspected; no reproduction of vendor benchmarks or complete line-by-line review.
